findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 3, Harm 3
Raise: Not done
Case: normal use - repos pinned to different Forge releases have runs active on the same machine when an upgrade is requested.
The advertised stop command cannot end a genuine pre-ID work run on POSIX. For example, v1.2.6 records a five-word local-time process identity (`v1.2.6:src/forge/codex.py:562`); current `src/forge/codex.py:910` treats that identity as unverifiable, so `src/forge/machine.py:648` refuses the printed stop command and the run continues to block upgrade. The legacy test copies identities from a current worker (`tests/test_upgrade_run_recovery.py:93`), so it misses this. Also, v1.2.46 CI events have no command field (`v1.2.46:src/forge/checks.py:138`), so `src/forge/upgrade.py:233` still identifies an earlier-release merge or merge-train wait as a close and gives the wrong resume command after ending it.

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Test
Case: normal use - a stopped intake returns its result while the coordinating session remains open.
The replacement test still does not prove that a refused handback releases a lane entry. Its preceding `forge stop --id` calls `native.cancel`, which already removes that entry (`src/forge/native.py:189-196`). Consequently, every assertion still passes if the new cleanup in `src/forge/native.py:216-221` is removed: the handback is refused with no entry left for it to release. The test therefore cannot catch the regression it names.
